description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of audio content categories in the MMAR benchmark dataset, which is designed to evaluate deep reasoning across speech, audio, music, and their mixtures. The chart is divided into seven segments, each representing a distinct audio type with its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “Speech,” occupying 29.4% of the chart, followed by “Music” at 20.6% and “Sound” at 16.5%. The “Mix-Sound-Speech” category accounts for 13.7% (inferred from the visible label “Mix-S...nd-Speech” and the missing percentage, which completes the total to 100%). The “Mix-Music-Speech” segment represents 8.2%, while “Mix-Sound-Music-Speech” and “Mix-Sound-Music” make up smaller portions at 2.4% and 1.1%, respectively. The segments are color-coded in varying shades of purple, with labels placed inside or adjacent to each slice, and the chart features a central white circle, giving it a donut-style appearance. The visual layout emphasizes the dominance of pure speech content, followed by music and sound, with mixed categories comprising a smaller but significant portion of the dataset.
